title: Serpentine Matrix Traversal (Alternating Rows)
prompt:
Implement `zigzag_matrix_rows(matrix) -> list[object]`. `matrix` is a rectangular list of rows. Visit every cell row by row: visit row 0 from left to right, row 1 from right to left, row 2 from left to right, and so on. Return the visited values as one flat list. This is an alternating-row (serpentine) traversal, not the diagonal zigzag traversal sometimes used in matrix problems.

Assume that the input matrix is rectangular. Do not print values or mutate the input. Aim for O(rows * cols) time and O(rows * cols) space for the returned list. This is a practice reconstruction of a reported Airbnb coding prompt; it supplies a return value so the interview idea can be run and verified.

example.reasoning: Rows are visited in alternating directions: left-to-right, right-to-left, then left-to-right.
